newsitem.title: USA: Five more immigrants die from cold, death toll 10.
newsitem.headline: Five more immigrants die from cold, death toll 10.

text.p: Five more illegal immigrants trying to cross from Mexico to California in bitterly cold weather have died of exposure, officials said on Thursday, bringing the death toll to at least 10 this week.
Dozens of illegal immigrants have recently surrendered to Border Patrol agents to escape sub-freezing temperatures after trying to shield themselves with large plastic bags.
The latest discovery was early on Thursday when Border Patrol agents found three bodies along a hiking trail in the Laguna Mountains, 70 miles (112.7 km) northeast of San Diego.

Salvador Zamora, a Border Patrol spokesman, said two immigrants who were stopped on Wednesday night in Cleveland National Forest told agents they were travelling with six others and had crossed the U.S./Mexican border east of Tecate. They said a member of their group had died in the cold.

On Wednesday, agents found the body of a male in the Otay Mesa area near the border south of San Diego, and U.S. Department of Forestry Service officers found the body of a male east of Buckman Springs, also in the Laguna mountains.
Three more bodies were found on Tuesday, including a woman and two men. A 17-year-old boy and a 21-year-old woman were found dead of exposure near Pine Valley on Monday.

Zamora said since the beginning of the year 13 illegal immigrants had died while crossing into the United States, all but two from exposure to the cold. The U.S. Weather Service reported that temperatures were expected to rise on Friday and through the weekend.
